key_insight: Incorporating semantic knowledge via Knowledge Graph Embeddings (KGEs) into Deep Reinforcement Learning significantly reduces the experience (samples) required to train robotic manipulators, enabling faster and more reliable policy learning.
problem_solved: Addresses DRL's sample inefficiency and high computational/time costs in robotic manipulation by providing contextual semantic priors that guide learning and exploration.
method: Encode task- and environment-level semantics as Knowledge Graph Embeddings and integrate them into the agent's observation or latent state.
Use semantic priors to shape exploration and/or augment the policy/value network input, reducing reliance on raw trial-and-error.
Evaluate the combined KGE+DRL pipeline on robotic manipulator tasks to demonstrate faster convergence and improved sample efficiency (with ablation to isolate KGE benefit).
impact: Makes DRL for robotics more practical by cutting training time and compute needs, improving sample efficiency and facilitating safer, more transferable policies for real-world manipulators.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Knowledge Graph -> KGE encoder -> DRL agent (policy/value networks) -> robot manipulator, showing information flow.
Learning curves: sample-efficiency plots comparing DRL vs KGE+DRL (faster convergence, fewer episodes).
Illustration of a manipulator with overlaid semantic graph (objects, relations, constraints) to show how semantics inform decisions.
Bar chart or table of ablation results highlighting performance gains attributable to the semantic component.
paper_title: Boosting Deep Reinforcement Learning with Semantic Knowledge for Robotic Manipulators
paper_authors: Lucía Güitta-López, Vincenzo Suriani, Jaime Boal, Álvaro J. López-López, Daniele Nardi
